newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Moody's says may review Sweden's debt ratings.
newsitem.headline: Moody's says may review Sweden's debt ratings.

text.p: U.S. credit ratings agency Moody's said on Thursday it may review the Kingdom of Sweden's sovereign debt ratings in 12 to 18 months for a possible upgrade.
"Sweden's rating is not up for review just now," Moody's Swedish analyst Kristin Lindow told Reuters.
"I do not exclude that it will come up for a survey for a possible upgrading in 12-18 months."
Moody's said there was a chance that Sweden's current foreign exchange debt rating of AA3, which was downgraded from AA2 in January 1995, could be lifted.
"There is a 50/50 chance that there will be an upgrade," Lindow said.
If Moody's at the review decided to upgrade Sweden's debt, it would take another another two or three months to change the rating, Lindow said.
"The situation in Sweden is more positive than negative," she said.

"What I am concerned about is the Swedish debt situation, not about the budget deficit per se. I think the budget deficit will decrease, but the question is how it is used. We want to see a trend and significant improvement in the Swedish indebtedness."
Another worry is the political situation with a general election due in September 1998.
"The timing of the election can come in the way for continued strict public finance policies," Lindow said.
Furthermore, Sweden's indecision about possible membership in Europe's Economic and Monetary Union (EMU) is also negative.
"A membership is important in view of Swedish credibility," she said.
